title: Loading in the browser
summary: Patch 0022 makes the browser build load reliably: twice the worker threads (the terrain's first patches no longer wait behind long jobs - loads now take 13 to 23 seconds instead of anything up to two and a half minutes), and a loading screen that waits for the world instead of giving up after half a minute.

steps.title: How it was measured
steps.text: The web build was served from this machine and played in Chromium, its frames counted from the page each second, its screen captured every few seconds, and - for a test build - the load's state printed to the browser's console once a second: whether the scene was built, and how many of each planet's first terrain patches were ready. Some loads took 15 s, others 140 s; the log showed why.

steps.title: Twice the worker threads
steps.text: Logged in the browser as it loaded: at times the terrain's first patch builds sat 140 s in the queue while the web build's four worker threads (the export's default) were all held by long jobs started at load. It now has eight, and the page sixteen threads: three loads in a row came in 13 to 23 seconds after Start game.

steps.title: The loading screen waits
steps.text: The browser's loading screen gave up after 30 seconds and left a dark screen while the world was still being built. There it now waits up to four minutes, its bar showing, till the game's ready; the desktop keeps its 30 seconds.

review.intro: The code behind patch 0022: the browser build's loading - its thread pools and its loading screen's patience.

files.explanation: Version 0.31's page for patch 0021 drawn properly: its text and a diagram of what it mended.

hunks.title: Patch 0021's page
hunks.note: The web build's fixes at a glance: the title, the loading screen, the terrain's instance slots, the sky.

files.explanation: The web build gets twice the worker threads: with the export's default four, long jobs started at load (towns, hulls, background loads) could hold them all and the terrain's first patches waited in the queue for up to 140 s.

hunks.title: Bigger thread pools
hunks.note: 8 worker threads for Godot's pool (was 4), 16 browser threads for the page (was 8).

bubbles.text: The WorkerThreadPool's threads in the browser: the terrain's patch builds no longer starve behind long jobs.

files.explanation: In a browser the loading screen waits up to four minutes for the world, not 30 s: it gave up before the world was built and left a dark screen.
